clip_script:
They call me the Science Queen. Watch what I do to exam stoichiometry.
[00:05] If your chemical equation is not balanced, your foundation is cracked. Every calculation that follows will be mathematically incorrect.
[00:15] Let us look at methane burning in oxygen. We must balance it. One carbon, four hydrogens, four oxygens. The ratio is one to two to one to two.
[00:25] Now, the balanced equation speaks in moles, not in grams. You cannot use a mass ratio directly.
[00:35] Look at your NSC data sheet. The formula is n equals m over M.
[00:45] Substitute explicitly into the formula. This is where the mark sheet gives substitution marks. Do not just write the final answer.
[00:55] That is how you secure full marks. Precision and correct formulas.
visual_style: Ms Dlamini at the whiteboard, striking and regal. High-contrast marker strokes showing the balancing and formula substitution step-by-step.
